newsitem.title: USA: At Home stock more than doubles after IPO.
newsitem.headline: At Home stock more than doubles after IPO.

text.p: Strong demand for shares of high-speed Internet access company At Home Corp. more than doubled the stock when it opened for trading on Friday.
The stock, which first opened near midday, leaped $13.25 to $23.75 from its IPO price of $10.50 a share.

Nine million shares were sold by the Redwood City, Calif., company, which provides a service that allows customers to hook up their PCs to the Internet over their existing cable television coaxial cables via cable modems.
The service is more than 300 times faster than typical dial-up modems, the company said in its prospectus.
At a stock price of $22, the company has a market capitalisation of $2.61 billion. It said it would have roughly 118.6 million shares outstanding after the IPO.
The shares were priced late Thursday. Morgan Stanley & Co. and Merrill Lynch were co-lead underwriters of the initial public offering.
The stock quickly vaulted to become one of the most active issues on the Nasdaq in its first minutes of trading, with over 3.6 million shares traded.
